articles.title: The Winter Olympics is also called the White Olympics
articles.fallbackTitle: The Winter Olympics is also called the White Olympics

blocks.text: The Winter Olympics is also called the White Olympics. At this time, many colorful stamps are published to mark the great Games. The first stamps marking the opening came out on January 25, 1932 in the United States for the 3rd White Olympics. From then on, publishing stamps during the White Olympics became a rule.
blocks.translation: 冬季奥运会也被称为“白色奥运会”。届时，许多色彩鲜艳的邮票会发行，以纪念这一体育盛会。第一套纪念奥运会开幕的邮票于 1932 年 1 月 25 日在美国发行，纪念第三届白色奥运会。从那时起，在白色奥运会期间发行邮票便成了一项惯例。

blocks.text: During the 4th Winter Olympic Games a group of stamps were published in Germany in November 1936. The five rings of Olympics were sewn(缝制)on the front of the sportswear. It was the first time that the rings appeared on the stamps of the White Olympics.
blocks.translation: 1936 年 11 月，德国发行了一组邮票纪念第四届冬季奥运会。奥运五环被缝制在运动服的前面。这是五环首次出现在白色奥运会的邮票上。

blocks.text: In the 1950’s, the stamps of this kind became more colorful. When the White Olympics came, the host countries as well as the non-host countries published stamps to mark those Games. China also published four stamps in February 1980, when the Chinese sportsmen began to take part in the White Olympics.
blocks.translation: 20 世纪 50 年代，这类邮票变得更加色彩丰富。白色奥运会举办时，主办国和非主办国都会发行邮票来纪念这些赛事。1980 年 2 月，当中国运动员开始参加白色奥运会时，中国也发行了四枚邮票。

blocks.text: Japan is the only Asian country that has ever held the White Olympics. Altogether 14, 500 million stamps were sold to raise money for this sports meet.
blocks.translation: 日本是唯一举办过白色奥运会的亚洲国家，共售出 145 亿枚邮票，为这届运动会筹集资金。

blocks.text: Different kinds of sports were drawn on these small stamps. People can enjoy the beauty of the wonderful movements of some sportsmen.
blocks.translation: 这些小邮票上绘制了各种不同的运动项目。人们可以欣赏到一些运动员优美动作的美感。

articles.title: Finally, the Christmas season is over
articles.fallbackTitle: Finally, the Christmas season is over

blocks.text: Finally, the Christmas season is over. We can take a long breath, put up our feet, sip from a cup of good tea and relax. The frenzy, starting from Black Friday right after Thanksgiving until Christmas Eve, of gift shopping, buying, wrapping, giving, receiving, opening, returning…is exhausting and time-consuming, but it takes place every year.
blocks.translation: 圣诞季终于结束了。我们可以长舒一口气，把脚翘起来，啜一口好茶，放松一下。从感恩节后的“黑色星期五”一直到圣诞前夜的这阵疯狂——买礼物、购物、包装、送礼、收礼、拆礼、退货……——既累人又费时，但每年都会上演。

blocks.text: There is considerable difference between the cultures in China and western countries when it comes to gift giving. In China, it is not polite to open a gift in front of the gift giver, and the gift is only looked at after the guest has left. Here in America, gift givers always wrap their gifts, large or small, priceless or valueless, carefully and decorate them with colorful ribbons and little pretty paper flowers; and the lucky receiver is expected to open the gift right away in front of the giver, with great eagerness and curiosity, and should always express appreciation with the all time truthful comment, “this is just exactly what I wanted!” Well, as a matter of fact, most people would take their “always wanted” gifts back to the store to exchange for something they really wanted.
blocks.translation: 在送礼这件事上，中国和西方国家的文化有相当大的差异。在中国，当着送礼人的面拆礼物是不礼貌的，礼物要等客人离开后才会被查看。而在美国，送礼人总会仔细包装礼物，无论大小、贵重与否，还会用彩色丝带和小巧的纸花装饰；幸运的收礼人则应当当着送礼人的面，带着极大的热切和好奇立刻打开礼物，并且总要表达赞赏，说一句永远“真实”的评价：“这正是我想要的！”嗯，事实上，大多数人会把他们“一直想要”的礼物拿回商店，换成自己真正想要的东西。

blocks.text: Finding a gift for somebody, even a close family member, you will have to know what the person likes and shop for days before you can locate the perfect gift. But, still the person may not like the gift from you. Nowadays, stores would provide two copies of the receipts for anything they sell as a gift, one of which is included in the gift package so that the receiver can come back for an exchange. I know, it was unthinkable to cash out the gift you get, but times are different. Another good way to avoid all that shopping hassle is to purchase a gift card from one of the stores and send it to your niece, nephews, or a family member, so that they can get whatever they want or even keep the money.
blocks.translation: 为别人找礼物，哪怕是关系亲密的家人，你也得知道对方喜欢什么，还要花好几天去逛，才能找到完美的礼物。但即便如此，对方可能还是不喜欢你送的礼物。如今，商店出售作为礼物的商品时通常会提供两份收据，其中一份放进礼物包装里，以便收礼人回来换货。我知道，把收到的礼物变现曾是不可想象的，但时代不同了。另一个避免这些购物麻烦的好办法是从某家商店买一张礼品卡，送给你的侄女、侄子或家人，这样他们就能想要什么买什么，甚至把钱留着。

paragraphs: Finally, the Christmas season is over. We can take a long breath, put up our feet, sip from a cup of good tea and relax. The frenzy, starting from Black Friday right after Thanksgiving until Christmas Eve, of gift shopping, buying, wrapping, giving, receiving, opening, returning…is exhausting and time-consuming, but it takes place every year.

There is considerable difference between the cultures in China and western countries when it comes to gift giving. In China, it is not polite to open a gift in front of the gift giver, and the gift is only looked at after the guest has left. Here in America, gift givers always wrap their gifts, large or small, priceless or valueless, carefully and decorate them with colorful ribbons and little pretty paper flowers; and the lucky receiver is expected to open the gift right away in front of the giver, with great eagerness and curiosity, and should always express appreciation with the all time truthful comment, “this is just exactly what I wanted!” Well, as a matter of fact, most people would take their “always wanted” gifts back to the store to exchange for something they really wanted.

Finding a gift for somebody, even a close family member, you will have to know what the person likes and shop for days before you can locate the perfect gift. But, still the person may not like the gift from you. Nowadays, stores would provide two copies of the receipts for anything they sell as a gift, one of which is included in the gift package so that the receiver can come back for an exchange. I know, it was unthinkable to cash out the gift you get, but times are different. Another good way to avoid all that shopping hassle is to purchase a gift card from one of the stores and send it to your niece, nephews, or a family member, so that they can get whatever they want or even keep the money.

articles.fallbackTitle: Are you interested in country music

blocks.text: Are you interested in country music? I like it very much! It will take me away for a while when I am tired. The guitars and songs will take me to the mountains and fields.
blocks.translation: 你对乡村音乐感兴趣吗？我非常喜欢它！疲惫的时候，它能带我离开一会儿。吉他和歌声会把我带到山间和田野。

blocks.text: Country music usually talks of everyday life and feeling. It’s the spirit of America, easy to understand, slow and simple.
blocks.translation: 乡村音乐通常歌唱日常生活和情感。它是美国的精神，通俗易懂，缓慢而简单。

blocks.text: Country music developed in the Southern United States. It was folk music of American countryside. Many songs tell about the lives of farmers. They talk about love, crops or death.
blocks.translation: 乡村音乐发展于美国南部。它是美国乡村的民间音乐。许多歌曲讲述农民的生活，唱的是爱情、庄稼或死亡。

blocks.text: The life of the countryside can be hard, so the words in country music are often sad. At first, people played the music only at family parties. But it became more popular later. In the 1920s, people played country songs on the radio and they made them into the records.
blocks.translation: 乡村生活可能很艰苦，所以乡村音乐的歌词常常带着忧伤。起初，人们只在家庭聚会上演奏这种音乐，后来它越来越受欢迎。20 世纪 20 年代，人们在广播里播放乡村歌曲，并把它们录成唱片。

blocks.text: When people in the countryside moved to towns and cities to look for work, they took their music with them. Country music continued to change and became popular across America.
blocks.translation: 当乡下人搬到城镇寻找工作时，他们把音乐也带到了那里。乡村音乐不断变化，并在全美流行起来。

blocks.text: John Denver was one of America’s most famous country singers in the 1970s. His song “Take Me Home, Country Roads ” is well-known and people still play it today.
blocks.translation: 约翰·丹佛是 20 世纪 70 年代美国最著名的乡村歌手之一。他的歌曲《乡村路带我回家》广为人知，至今仍被人们传唱。

articles.title: In ancient times wealth was measured and exchanged in things that could be touched: food,
articles.fallbackTitle: In ancient times wealth was measured and exchanged in things that could be touched: food,

blocks.text: In ancient times wealth was measured and exchanged in things that could be touched: food, tools, and precious metals and stones. Then the barter system was replaced by coins, which still had real value since they were pieces of rare metal. Coins were followed by fiat money, paper notes that have value only because everyone agrees to accept them.
blocks.translation: 在古代，财富是用可以触摸的东西来衡量和交换的：食物、工具以及贵金属和宝石。后来，以物易物制度被硬币取代，硬币仍然具有真实价值，因为它们是由稀有金属制成的。继硬币之后出现的是法定货币，即纸币，它之所以有价值，只是因为大家都同意接受它。

blocks.text: Today electronic monetary systems are gradually being introduced that will transform money into even less tangible forms, reducing it to a series of “bits and bytes”, or units of computerized information, going between machines at the speed of light. Already, electronic fund transfer allows money to be instantly sent and received by different banks, companies, and countries through computers and telecommunications devices.
blocks.translation: 如今，电子货币系统正逐渐被引入，它将把货币变成更加无形的形式，使其简化为一系列“比特和字节”，即计算机化信息的单位，以光速在机器之间传递。电子资金转账已经可以让资金通过计算机和电信设备在不同银行、公司和国家之间即时收发。

articles.title: Some people hate everything that is modern
articles.fallbackTitle: Some people hate everything that is modern

blocks.text: Some people hate everything that is modern. They cannot imagine how anyone can really like modern music; they find it hard to accept the new fashions in clothing; they think that all modern paintings are ugly; and they seldom have a good word for the new buildings that are being built everywhere in the world. Such people look for perfection in everything, and they take their standards of perfection from the past. They are usually impatient with anyone who is brave enough to experiment with new things or to express himself or the age in original ways.
blocks.translation: 有些人憎恨一切现代的东西。他们无法想象怎么会有人真的喜欢现代音乐；他们觉得很难接受新款式的服装；他们认为所有现代绘画都很丑；对于世界各地正在建造的新建筑，他们也很少说一句好话。这样的人凡事都追求完美，而他们的完美标准来自过去。对于那些勇于尝试新事物或以原创方式表达自我、表达时代的人，他们通常很不耐烦。

blocks.text: It is, of course, true that many artists do not succeed in their work and instead produce works that can only be considered as failures. If the work of art is a painting, the artist’s failure concerns himself alone, but if it is a building, his failure concerns others too. Because it may damage the beauty of the whole place. This does sometimes happen, but it is completely untrue to say, as some people do, that modern architecture is nothing.
blocks.translation: 当然，许多艺术家确实没有在作品中取得成功，反而创作出只能被视为失败的作品。如果艺术作品是一幅画，艺术家的失败只关乎他自己；但如果是一座建筑，他的失败也会影响别人，因为它可能破坏整个地方的美感。这种情况确实有时会发生，但像有些人那样说现代建筑一无是处，则是完全不正确的。

blocks.text: We can’t judge every modern building by the standards of the ancient time, even though we admire the ancient buildings. Technologically, the modern buildings are more advanced. The modern architect knows he should learn from the ancient works, but with his greater resources of knowledge and materials, he will never be content to imitate the past. He is too proud to do that.
blocks.translation: 即使我们欣赏古代建筑，也不能用古代的标准来评判每一座现代建筑。从技术上讲，现代建筑更先进。现代建筑师知道自己应该向古代作品学习，但凭借更丰富的知识和材料资源，他绝不会满足于模仿过去。他太骄傲了，不会那样做。

articles.title: Anthropology (人类学) is the study of how people live
articles.fallbackTitle: Anthropology (人类学) is the study of how people live

blocks.text: Anthropology (人类学) is the study of how people live. It includes their family life, religion, laws and language. The term “anthropology” comes from two Greek words: “anthropos” means “human being” and “logy” means “the science of”. Anthropology can be divided into two areas. These two main divisions are cultural anthropology and physical anthropology.
blocks.translation: 人类学是研究人们如何生活的学科。它包括人们的家庭生活、宗教、法律和语言。“anthropology”一词来自两个希腊词：“anthropos”意为“人”，“logy”意为“……学”。人类学可分为两个领域，这两个主要分支是文化人类学和体质人类学。

blocks.text: Anthropologists define human progress in three main steps. Step one begins with the first human being and continues until the last of people who hunted animals just to survive. Step two includes people who grew food. In this step, there was progress in invention and religion. Step three deals with first civilizations, such as those in Egypt and parts of Asia.
blocks.translation: 人类学家把人类进步划分为三个主要阶段。第一阶段从最早的人类开始，一直延续到最后一批只为生存而猎捕动物的人。第二阶段包括种植食物的人。在这一阶段，发明和宗教都有所进步。第三阶段涉及最早的文明，例如埃及和亚洲部分地区的文明。

blocks.text: Anthropologists always seek new information about people. For instance, recent evidence found in Ethiopia and Kenya shows humans existed earlier in history than it was previously believed.
blocks.translation: 人类学家总是寻求关于人的新信息。例如，最近在埃塞俄比亚和肯尼亚发现的证据表明，人类在历史上存在的时间比人们以前认为的更早。

These two main divisions are cultural anthropology and physical anthropology.

Anthropologists define human progress in three main steps. Step one begins with the first human being and continues until the last of people who hunted animals just to survive. Step two includes people who grew food. In this step, there was progress in invention and religion. Step three deals with first civilizations, such as those in Egypt and parts of Asia.

articles.title: Ancient people had little idea of the nature of the earth’s surface
articles.fallbackTitle: Ancient people had little idea of the nature of the earth’s surface

blocks.text: Ancient people had little idea of the nature of the earth’s surface. But if they lived on the seashore, they knew that there was land and sea.
blocks.translation: 古人对地球表面的性质几乎一无所知。但如果他们住在海边，他们就知道有陆地和海洋。

blocks.text: People who lived near the sea noticed that there were two kinds of land. There were, first, little pieces of land surrounded by sea. One Latin word for “sea” is “salum”, which means “salt”. This is because sea water, unlike rain-water, contains salt – it is salty. So a piece of land in the sea was “in salt” in Latin, and this became isle in English.
blocks.translation: 住在海边的人注意到有两种陆地。首先是被海水环绕的小块陆地。拉丁语中表示“海”的一个词是“salum”，意思是“盐”。这是因为海水与雨水不同，含有盐分——它是咸的。因此，海中的一块陆地在拉丁语中是“in salt”，这在英语中变成了 isle（小岛）。

blocks.text: Then there was another kind of land that went on and on. It was “continuous land”, and so became known as continent in English from the Latin “continens” meaning continuous. In English, we also speak of a continent as the mainland ( “main” comes from the Latin “magnus” meaning “great”), as opposed to island (isle-land).
blocks.translation: 还有另一种陆地，绵延不断。它是“连续不断的陆地”，因此在英语中被称为 continent，源自拉丁语“continens”，意为“连续的”。在英语中，我们还把大陆称为 mainland（“main”来自拉丁语“magnus”，意为“伟大的”），与 island（isle-land，岛屿）相对。

blocks.text: To the ancient Greek, there seemed to be three continents separated by sea. The Mediterranean Sea, in fact, gets its name from the Latin “medius” (middle) and “terra” (land). It was a sea that lay in the middle, with three bodies of land around it. The three continents — Asia, Europe and Africa — are actually connected by land. Africa and Asia are connected by only the small Sinai Isthmus, from the Greek “isthmus” meaning “a narrow passage”, but Europe and Asia are connected by land for a thousand miles or more and it is customary to speak of Europe as a continent. Many geographers speak of the landmass of Asia plus Europe as Eurasia, and Eurasia plus Africa is sometimes called the World Island. The three together are surrounded by sea, so they form a large island, and they contain about 85 percent of the earth’s population.
blocks.translation: 在古希腊人看来，似乎有三块被海洋分隔的大陆。事实上，地中海（Mediterranean）这个名字来自拉丁语“medius”（中间）和“terra”（陆地）。它是一片位于中间的海，周围环绕着三块陆地。三大洲——亚洲、欧洲和非洲——实际上由陆地相连。非洲和亚洲只由小小的西奈地峡相连，地峡（isthmus）一词来自希腊语，意为“狭窄的通道”；而欧洲和亚洲由陆地相连长达一千多英里，因此习惯上把欧洲称为一个大陆。许多地理学家把亚洲和欧洲的陆块合称为欧亚大陆，欧亚大陆加上非洲有时被称为“世界岛”。这三块大陆合在一起被海洋环绕，因此构成一个巨大的岛屿，拥有地球上约 85% 的人口。

paragraphs: Ancient people had little idea of the nature of the earth’s surface. But if they lived on the seashore, they knew that there was land and sea.

People who lived near the sea noticed that there were two kinds of land. There were, first, little pieces of land surrounded by sea. One Latin word for “sea” is “salum”, which means “salt”. This is because sea water, unlike rain-water, contains salt – it is salty. So a piece of land in the sea was “in salt” in Latin, and this became isle in English.

Then there was another kind of land that went on and on. It was “continuous land”, and so became known as continent in English from the Latin “continens” meaning continuous. In English, we also speak of a continent as the mainland ( “main” comes from the Latin “magnus” meaning “great”), as opposed to island (isle-land).

To the ancient Greek, there seemed to be three continents separated by sea. The Mediterranean Sea, in fact, gets its name from the Latin “medius” (middle) and “terra” (land). It was a sea that lay in the middle, with three bodies of land around it. The three continents — Asia, Europe and Africa — are actually connected by land. Africa and Asia are connected by only the small Sinai Isthmus, from the Greek “isthmus” meaning “a narrow passage”, but Europe and Asia are connected by land for a thousand miles or more and it is customary to speak of Europe as a continent. Many geographers speak of the landmass of Asia plus Europe as Eurasia, and Eurasia plus Africa is sometimes called the World Island. The three together are surrounded by sea, so they form a large island, and they contain about 85 percent of the earth’s population.

articles.title: Benjamin Franklin was born in 1706 in Boston, Massachusetts
articles.fallbackTitle: Benjamin Franklin was born in 1706 in Boston, Massachusetts

blocks.text: Benjamin Franklin was born in 1706 in Boston, Massachusetts. His mother and father were Puritans (清教徒). They left England and moved to the English colony of Massachusetts in order to escape persecution (迫害) for their religion. In Boston, Franklin left school when he was ten years old and worked for his father for two years. Then he went to work on his brother’s newspaper. He became the editor of this paper when he was sixteen. Because he wanted to be independent, he went to Philadelphia. There he began his own newspaper. He worked hard and saved his money. And by the age of 24, he was one of the most successful men in Philadelphia.
blocks.translation: 本杰明·富兰克林 1706 年出生于马萨诸塞州的波士顿。他的父母是清教徒。为了逃避宗教迫害，他们离开英国，搬到英国殖民地马萨诸塞。在波士顿，富兰克林十岁时辍学，为父亲工作了两年。之后他去哥哥的报社工作，十六岁时成为这份报纸的编辑。因为想要独立，他去了费城。在那里，他创办了自己的报纸。他努力工作，节省开支。到 24 岁时，他已成为费城最成功的人士之一。

blocks.text: In 1732, Franklin published a book Poor Richard’s Almanac (穷理查年鉴). Most almanacs contained information for farmers, such as information about the days and weeks of the year and about the weather. To his almanacs, Franklin added wise sayings and his observations about life. Some of these sayings are still famous today. For example, “Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise.” “Waste not, want not.” and “A penny saved is a penny earned.”
blocks.translation: 1732 年，富兰克林出版了《穷理查年鉴》。大多数年鉴包含供农民使用的信息，比如一年中的日期、周次以及天气信息。富兰克林在自己的年鉴中加入了格言和对生活的观察。其中一些格言至今仍然著名，例如：“早睡早起使人健康、富有、明智。”“不浪费，不愁缺。”以及“省下一便士就是赚到一便士。”

blocks.text: For millions of people around the world, the very word “Christmas” brings warmth and joy to their hearts and homes. To some, it is simply a very popular holiday. But for many, it honors the birth of Jesus Christ. Here is a brief history of Christmas, and some of the traditions connected with it.
blocks.translation: 对全世界数百万人来说，“圣诞节”这个词本身就给他们的心灵和家庭带来温暖与欢乐。对一些人来说，它只是一个很受欢迎的节日；但对许多人来说，它是纪念耶稣基督的诞生。以下是圣诞节的简史，以及与之相关的一些传统。

blocks.text: Why December 25th?
blocks.translation: 为什么是 12 月 25 日？

blocks.text: Well, during the first two centuries after Jesus’ death, Christmas was not celebrated at all. Various attempts were made to determine the date of birth of Jesus, and at first, May 20th became the favored date. By the middle of the fourth century, however, Pope Julius selected December 25th as the day on which to celebrate Christ’s birth. Before that, December 25th had been a widely celebrated day in the Roman world. On that date, people honored a Roman sun god. Many modern Christmas customs, such as having a tree in the house and preparing special meals, came from this ancient celebration.
blocks.translation: 在耶稣去世后的最初两个世纪里，人们根本不庆祝圣诞节。人们曾多次尝试确定耶稣的出生日期，起初 5 月 20 日成为受青睐的日期。然而到四世纪中叶，教皇尤利乌斯选定 12 月 25 日作为庆祝基督诞生的日子。在此之前，12 月 25 日在罗马世界已是一个广泛庆祝的日子。在那一天，人们纪念罗马的太阳神。许多现代圣诞习俗，比如在家里摆一棵树、准备特别的饭菜，都来自这一古老的庆祝活动。

blocks.text: Let’s decorate the tree!
blocks.translation: 我们来装饰圣诞树吧！

blocks.text: The Christmas tree tradition was started in Germany in the late fifteenth century. At that time, there was a popular theater play which included a fir tree hung with apples. Today, more than 80 percent of American families buy and decorate a tree at Christmas.
blocks.translation: 圣诞树的传统始于 15 世纪末的德国。当时有一出很受欢迎的戏剧，剧中有一棵挂着苹果的冷杉树。如今，超过 80% 的美国家庭会在圣诞节购买并装饰圣诞树。

blocks.text: How many Christmas cards do you usually send?
blocks.translation: 你通常寄多少张圣诞贺卡？

blocks.text: The first commercial Christmas cards were made in London in 1843. A rich man paid an artist to design a card. He then proudly sent it to his friends and relatives to wish them a “Merry Christmas”. It was a good idea and it soon caught on. Today, Americans exchange millions of Christmas cards every year.
blocks.translation: 第一批商业圣诞贺卡于 1843 年在伦敦制作。一位富人花钱请艺术家设计了一张贺卡，然后自豪地寄给亲友，祝他们“圣诞快乐”。这是个好主意，很快流行起来。如今，美国人每年交换数百万张圣诞贺卡。

blocks.text: Santa Claus is coming to town!
blocks.translation: 圣诞老人进城啦！

blocks.text: St. Nicholas was the original Santa Claus or “Father Christmas”. He was widely known as a kind man who loved children. After his death, a story developed that he used to visit children on Christmas Eve and give them presents. When the Dutch people came to live in America many years ago, they brought their St. Nicholas, or Sinterklaas in Dutch, with them. Sinterklaas is therefore where we get the name Santa Claus.
blocks.translation: 圣尼古拉斯就是最初的圣诞老人，或称“圣诞之父”。他广为人知，是一位喜爱孩子的善良之人。他去世后，流传出一个故事，说他常在圣诞前夜探望孩子并送他们礼物。许多年前荷兰人来到美国定居时，也带来了他们的圣尼古拉斯，荷兰语叫 Sinterklaas。Santa Claus 这个名字正是由 Sinterklaas 演变而来。

blocks.text: What’s in that stocking?
blocks.translation: 圣诞袜里装的是什么？

blocks.text: According to the story, the practice of hanging up stockings is connected with St. Nicholas. It is believed that St. Nicholas learned about a man who was hopelessly in debt. He also learned that the man and his daughters were about to be sold as slaves. Nicholas went to the man’s home at night and threw a bag of gold through the man’s window. The bag of gold landed in one of the daughters’ stockings that had been hung up to dry.
blocks.translation: 根据传说，挂圣诞袜的习俗与圣尼古拉斯有关。据说圣尼古拉斯得知有一个人债台高筑、走投无路，还得知这个人和他的女儿们即将被卖为奴隶。尼古拉斯夜里来到那人家中，从窗户扔进一袋金币。这袋金币正好落进其中一个女儿挂起来晾干的袜子里。

blocks.text: Today, all the above traditions are still kept as ways of celebrating Christmas.
blocks.translation: 如今，上述所有传统仍作为庆祝圣诞节的方式保留着。

paragraphs: For millions of people around the world, the very word “Christmas” brings warmth and joy to their hearts and homes. To some, it is simply a very popular holiday. But for many, it honors the birth of Jesus Christ. Here is a brief history of Christmas, and some of the traditions connected with it.
Why December 25th?

Well, during the first two centuries after Jesus’ death, Christmas was not celebrated at all. Various attempts were made to determine the date of birth of Jesus, and at first, May 20th became the favored date. By the middle of the fourth century, however, Pope Julius selected December 25th as the day on which to celebrate Christ’s birth. Before that, December 25th had been a widely celebrated day in the Roman world. On that date, people honored a Roman sun god. Many modern Christmas customs, such as having a tree in the house and preparing special meals, came from this ancient celebration.
Let’s decorate the tree!

The Christmas tree tradition was started in Germany in the late fifteenth century. At that time, there was a popular theater play which included a fir tree hung with apples. Today, more than 80 percent of American families buy and decorate a tree at Christmas.
How many Christmas cards do you usually send?

The first commercial Christmas cards were made in London in 1843. A rich man paid an artist to design a card. He then proudly sent it to his friends and relatives to wish them a “Merry Christmas”. It was a good idea and it soon caught on. Today, Americans exchange millions of Christmas cards every year.
Santa Claus is coming to town!

St. Nicholas was the original Santa Claus or “Father Christmas”. He was widely known as a kind man who loved children. After his death, a story developed that he used to visit children on Christmas Eve and give them presents. When the Dutch people came to live in America many years ago, they brought their St. Nicholas, or Sinterklaas in Dutch, with them. Sinterklaas is therefore where we get the name Santa Claus.
What’s in that stocking?

According to the story, the practice of hanging up stockings is connected with St. Nicholas. It is believed that St. Nicholas learned about a man who was hopelessly in debt. He also learned that the man and his daughters were about to be sold as slaves. Nicholas went to the man’s home at night and threw a bag of gold through the man’s window. The bag of gold landed in one of the daughters’ stockings that had been hung up to dry.
Today, all the above traditions are still kept as ways of celebrating Christmas.

articles.fallbackTitle: On November 19, 1863, Abraham Lincoln went to Gettysburg in Pennsylvania to speak at the N

blocks.text: On November 19, 1863, Abraham Lincoln went to Gettysburg in Pennsylvania to speak at the National Soldiers Cemetery. The Civil War was still going on. There was much criticism of President Lincoln at the time. He was not at all popular. He had been invited to speak at Gettysburg only out of courtesy. The principal speaker was to be Edward Everett, a famous statesman and speaker of the day. Everett was a handsome man and very popular everywhere.
blocks.translation: 1863 年 11 月 19 日，亚伯拉罕·林肯前往宾夕法尼亚州的葛底斯堡，在国家士兵公墓发表演讲。当时内战仍在进行。那时人们对林肯总统有很多批评，他一点也不受欢迎。他受邀到葛底斯堡演讲只是出于礼节。主要演讲者是当时著名的政治家和演说家爱德华·埃弗雷特。埃弗雷特相貌英俊，到处都很受欢迎。

blocks.text: It is said that Lincoln prepared his speech on the train while going to Gettysburg. Late that night, alone in his hotel room and tired out, he again worked briefly on the speech. The next day Everett spoke first. He spoke for an hour and 57 minutes. His speech was a perfect example of the rich oratory of the day. Then Lincoln rose. The crowd of 15,000 people at first paid little attention to him. He spoke for only nine minutes. At the end there was little applause. Lincoln turned to a friend and remarked, “I have failed again.” On the train back to Washington he commented sadly, “That speech was a flat failure, and the people are disappointed.”

paragraphs: On November 19, 1863, Abraham Lincoln went to Gettysburg in Pennsylvania to speak at the National Soldiers Cemetery. The Civil War was still going on. There was much criticism of President Lincoln at the time. He was not at all popular. He had been invited to speak at Gettysburg only out of courtesy. The principal speaker was to be Edward Everett, a famous statesman and speaker of the day. Everett was a handsome man and very popular everywhere.

It is said that Lincoln prepared his speech on the train while going to Gettysburg. Late that night, alone in his hotel room and tired out, he again worked briefly on the speech. The next day Everett spoke first. He spoke for an hour and 57 minutes. His speech was a perfect example of the rich oratory of the day. Then Lincoln rose. The crowd of 15,000 people at first paid little attention to him. He spoke for only nine minutes. At the end there was little applause. Lincoln turned to a friend and remarked, “I have failed again.” On the train back to Washington he commented sadly, “That speech was a flat failure, and the people are disappointed.”

It was a speech which only Abraham Lincoln could have made. Today, every American school child learns Lincoln’s Gettysburg Address by heart. Now everyone thinks of it as one of the greatest orations ever given in American history.

articles.fallbackTitle: In 1939 two brothers, Mac and Dick McDonald, started a drive-in restaurant in San Bernadin

blocks.text: In 1939 two brothers, Mac and Dick McDonald, started a drive-in restaurant in San Bernadino, California. They carefully chose a busy corner for their location. They had run their own businesses for years, first a theater, then a barbecue (烤肉) restaurant, then another drive-in. But in their new operation, they offered a new, shortened menu: French fries, hamburgers, and sodas. To this small selection they added one new concept: quick service, no waiters or waitresses, and no tips. Their hamburgers sold for fifteen cents. Cheese was another four cents. Their French fries and hamburgers had a remarkable uniformity, for the brothers had developed a strict routine for the preparation of their food, and they insisted on their cooks’ sticking to their routine. Their new drive-in became incredibly popular, particularly for lunch. People drove up by the hundreds during the busy noon time. The self-service restaurant was so popular that the brothers had allowed ten copies of their restaurant to be opened. They were content with this modest success until they met Ray Kroc.
blocks.translation: 1939 年，麦克和迪克·麦当劳两兄弟在加利福尼亚州圣贝纳迪诺开了一家汽车餐厅。他们精心挑选了一个繁忙的街角作为店址。他们经营自己的生意已有多年，先是一家剧院，然后是烤肉餐厅，再后来又是一家汽车餐厅。但在新的事业中，他们提供了一份新的、精简的菜单：炸薯条、汉堡包和汽水。在这个小小的选择之外，他们还加入了一个新理念：快速服务，没有服务员，也不收小费。他们的汉堡卖 15 美分，加奶酪再加 4 美分。他们的炸薯条和汉堡包有着惊人的一致性，因为兄弟俩为食物制作制定了严格的流程，并坚持让厨师严格遵守。他们的新汽车餐厅变得极其受欢迎，尤其是午餐时间。忙碌的中午，成百上千的人开车前来。这家自助餐厅如此受欢迎，以至于兄弟俩允许开设了十家分店。他们对这种小小的成功很满足，直到遇见了雷·克罗克。

blocks.text: Kroc was a salesman who met the McDonald brothers in 1954, when he was selling milk shake-mixing machines. He quickly saw the unique appeal of the brothers’ fast-food restaurants and bought the right to franchise（特许经营）other copies of their restaurants. The agreement struck included the right to duplicate the menu, the equipment, even their red and white buildings with the golden arches（拱门）.
blocks.translation: 克罗克是一名推销员，1954 年他在推销奶昔搅拌机时结识了麦当劳兄弟。他很快看出了兄弟俩快餐店的独特吸引力，并买下了特许经营其他分店的权利。双方达成的协议包括复制菜单、设备，甚至包括他们那带有金色拱门的红白建筑的权利。

blocks.text: Today McDonald’s is really a household name. Its names for its sandwiches have come to mean hamburger in the decades since the day Ray Kroc watched people rush up to order fifteen-cent hamburgers. In 1976, McDonald’s had over $1 billion in total sales. Its first twenty-two years is one of the most incredible success stories in modern American business history.
blocks.translation: 如今，麦当劳真的成了一个家喻户晓的名字。自从雷·克罗克看着人们蜂拥而来购买 15 美分汉堡的那天起，几十年间，麦当劳对其三明治的称呼已经成了汉堡包的代名词。1976 年，麦当劳的总销售额超过 10 亿美元。它最初的二十二年是现代美国商业史上最不可思议的成功故事之一。

articles.fallbackTitle: When young people get their first real jobs, they face a lot of new and confusing situatio

blocks.text: When young people get their first real jobs, they face a lot of new and confusing situations. They may find that everything is different from the way things were at school. It is also possible that they will feel uncomfortable and insecure in both professional and social situations. Eventually, they realize that university classes can’t be the only preparation for all of the different situations that arise in the working world.
blocks.translation: 年轻人找到第一份真正的工作时，会面临许多新情况，令人困惑。他们可能会发现，一切都与学校里的情况不同。他们也可能会在职业场合和社交场合感到不自在、缺乏安全感。最终，他们意识到，大学课程不可能是为职场中出现的各种不同情况所做的唯一准备。

blocks.text: Perhaps the best way to learn how to behave in the working world is to identify a worker you admire and observe his behavior. By doing so, you will be able to see what it is that you admire in this person. For example, you will observe how he acts in a crisis. Perhaps even more importantly, you will be able to see what his approach to day-to-day situations is.
blocks.translation: 也许，学习如何在职场中行事的最好方法，是找一位你钦佩的同事，观察他的行为。这样做，你就能看清自己究竟钦佩这个人的什么。例如，你会观察他在危机中如何行事。也许更重要的是，你能看到他对日常情况采取什么方式。

blocks.text: While you are observing your colleague, you should be asking yourself whether his behavior is like yours and how you can learn from his responses to a variety of situations. By watching and learning from a model, you will probably begin to identify and adopt good working habits.
blocks.translation: 在观察同事的同时，你应该问自己：他的行为是否与你相似？你能如何从他应对各种情况的反应中学习？通过观察榜样并向其学习，你大概会开始识别并养成好的工作习惯。

paragraphs: When young people get their first real jobs, they face a lot of new and confusing situations. They may find that everything is different from the way things were at school. It is also possible that they will feel uncomfortable and insecure in both professional and social situations. Eventually, they realize that university classes can’t be the only preparation for all of the different situations that arise in the working world.

Perhaps the best way to learn how to behave in the working world is to identify a worker you admire and observe his behavior. By doing so, you will be able to see what it is that you admire in this person. For example, you will observe how he acts in a crisis. Perhaps even more importantly, you will be able to see what his approach to day-to-day situations is.

While you are observing your colleague, you should be asking yourself whether his behavior is like yours and how you can learn from his responses to a variety of situations. By watching and learning from a model, you will probably begin to identify and adopt good working habits.

blocks.text: Airline companies are responsible for transporting your luggage. If you cannot recover it at the point of arrival, you must inform the airline immediately. They will carry out the necessary search. If the luggage is recovered, it will be delivered to your place of residence. If you wish to insure your luggage, you may do so at your own expense.
blocks.translation: 航空公司负责运送你的行李。如果你在抵达地点无法取回行李，必须立即通知航空公司。他们会进行必要的查找。如果行李被找回，将会送到你的住处。如果你希望为行李投保，可以自费办理。

blocks.text: Some airlines restrict luggage weight to 44 pounds(20 kg); in other cases, there is no weight restriction, but you are not allowed more than two pieces of luggage. questions.explanation: 全文讲行李的查找、重量限制、超重付费、标签填写等处理办法，最全面的概括是 the handling of your luggage。

translations: 航空公司负责运送你的行李。如果你在抵达地点无法取回行李，必须立即通知航空公司。他们会进行必要的查找。如果行李被找回，将会送到你的住处。如果你希望为行李投保，可以自费办理。
有些航空公司把行李重量限制在 44 磅（20 公斤）；另一些则没有重量限制，但不允许携带超过两件行李。请向你将乘坐的航空公司咨询行李额度。不过，超重行李必须额外付费，加拿大国际开发署（CIDA）不予补偿。
每个手提箱、包或包裹都必须清楚地标明你的姓名和目的地。如果你出发时不知道确切的目的地地址，可以在行李标签上写明由培训协议中列明的执行机构代收，格式如下：
姓氏，名字；你所在国家的名称；执行机构的地址；城市、国家、邮政编码；执行机构的电话号码
如果你没有这些信息，请用你在加拿大所要就读机构的名称和地址来标注行李。如果这些信息都没有，可以使用 CIDA 的地址。

articles.title: I am one of the many city people who are always saying that given the choice we would pref
articles.fallbackTitle: I am one of the many city people who are always saying that given the choice we would pref

blocks.text: I am one of the many city people who are always saying that given the choice we would prefer to live in the country away from the dirt and noise of a large city. I have managed to convince myself that if it weren’t for my job I would immediately head out for the open spaces and go back to nature in some sleepy village buried in the country. But how realistic is the dream?
blocks.translation: 我是许多城里人中的一个，我们总说：如果有得选，我们宁愿住在乡下，远离大城市的污浊和喧嚣。我说服了自己：要不是为了工作，我会立刻奔向开阔的天地，回到某个沉睡在乡间的小村庄，回归自然。但这个梦想有多现实呢？

blocks.text: Cities can be frightening places. The majority of the population live in massive tower blocks, noisy, dirty and impersonal. The sense of belonging to a community tends to disappear when you live fifteen floors up. All you can see from your window is sky, or other blocks of flats. Children become aggressive and nervous — cooped up at home all day, with nowhere to play; their mothers feel isolated from the rest of the world. Strangely enough, whereas in the past the inhabitants of one street all knew each other, nowadays people on the same floor in tower blocks don’t even say hello to each other.
blocks.translation: 城市可能是令人恐惧的地方。大多数人口住在巨大的高楼里，嘈杂、肮脏而且冷漠。当你住在十五层楼以上时，对社区的归属感往往会消失。从窗口只能看到天空或别的公寓楼。孩子们变得好斗、紧张——整天被关在家里，没有地方玩；他们的母亲感到与外界隔绝。奇怪的是，过去一条街上的人都互相认识，而如今同一层楼的人甚至彼此连招呼都不打。

blocks.text: Country life, on the other hand, differs from this kind of isolated existence in that a sense of community generally binds the inhabitants of small villages together. People have the advantage of knowing that there is always someone to turn to when they need help. But country life has disadvantages too. While it is true that you may be among friends in a village, it is also true that you are cut off from the existing and important events that take place in cities. There’s little possibility of going to a new show or the latest movie. Shopping becomes a major problem, and for anything slightly out of the ordinary you have to go on an expedition to the nearest large town. The city-dweller who leaves for the country is often oppressed by a sense of unbearable stillness and quiet.
blocks.translation: 另一方面，乡村生活与这种孤立的存在不同，因为一种社区感通常把一个小村庄的居民联系在一起。人们有一个好处：知道自己需要帮助时总有人可以求助。但乡村生活也有缺点。虽然你在村里可能置身于朋友之中，但你也确实与城市里发生的重要事件隔绝。去看一场新演出或最新电影的机会很少。购物成了大问题，稍微不寻常一点的东西都得跑到最近的大城镇去采购。离开城市去乡下的人，常常被一种难以忍受的寂静压得喘不过气。

blocks.text: What, then, is the answer? The country has the advantage of peace and quiet, but suffers from the disadvantage of being cut off; the city breeds a feeling of isolation, and constant noise batters the senses. But one of its main advantages is that you are at the center of things, and that life doesn’t come to an end at half-past nine at night. Some people have found (or rather bought) a compromise between the two: they have expressed their preference for the “quiet life” by leaving the suburbs and moving to villages within commuting distance of large cities. They generally have about as much sensitivity as the plastic flowers they leave behind — they are polluted with strange ideas about change and improvement which they force on to the unwilling original inhabitants of the villages.
blocks.translation: 那么，答案是什么呢？乡村有宁静的好处，却有与世隔绝的缺点；城市滋生孤立感，持续的噪音冲击着感官。但城市的主要优点之一是，你身处事物的中心，生活不会在晚上九点半就结束。有些人找到了（或者说买到了）两者之间的折中：他们选择“安静的生活”，离开郊区，搬到离大城市通勤距离内的村庄。他们的敏感程度大概和他们留下的塑料花差不多——他们满脑子奇怪的想法，想要“改变”和“改善”，并把这些强加给不情愿的原有村民。

blocks.text: What then of my dreams of leaning on a cottage gate and murmuring “morning” to the locals as they pass by? I’m keen on the idea, but you see there’s my cat, Toby. I’m not at all sure that he would take to all that fresh air and exercise in the long grass. I mean, can you see him mixing with all those hearty males down the farm? No, he would rather have the electric imitation-coal fire any evening.
blocks.translation: 那么，我倚在村舍门前，对着路过的当地人低声说“早上好”的梦想又怎样呢？我很喜欢这个想法，但你知道，我还有我的猫托比。我完全不确定它会不会喜欢那么多新鲜空气和在深草丛里的运动。我的意思是，你能想象它和农场里那些健壮的雄性动物打成一片吗？不，它宁愿每天晚上守着那台电动的仿煤火炉。

articles.title: Ideas about education are changing in the United States
articles.fallbackTitle: Ideas about education are changing in the United States

blocks.text: Ideas about education are changing in the United States. Education today is not just a high school diploma or a college degree. Many adults are not interested in going to college. They are interested in other kinds of learning. For them, learning does not end with a diploma.
blocks.translation: 在美国，关于教育的观念正在发生变化。今天的教育不只是一张高中文凭或大学学位。许多成年人对上大学不感兴趣，他们感兴趣的是其他种类的学习。对他们来说，学习并不会随着拿到文凭而结束。

blocks.text: Continuing education gives these adults the opportunity to increase their knowledge about their own field or to learn about a new field. It also gives them a chance to improve their old skills or to learn new ones.
blocks.translation: 继续教育让这些成年人有机会增进本领域的知识，或学习一个新的领域。它也给他们机会提高旧技能或学习新技能。

blocks.text: Scientists, mechanics and barbers can take classes to improve their work skills. If they know more or learn more, they can get a better job or earn more money.
blocks.translation: 科学家、机械师和理发师都可以上课来提高工作技能。如果他们懂得更多、学得更多，就能得到更好的工作或挣更多的钱。

blocks.text: Continuing education classes give more adults the chances to learn new skills. There is usually a large variety of classes to choose from: typing, foreign cooking, photography, auto repair, furniture repair, or swimming. These are only some of the classes available.
blocks.translation: 继续教育课程让更多成年人有机会学习新技能。通常有各种各样的课程可供选择：打字、外国烹饪、摄影、汽车修理、家具修理或游泳。这些只是可选课程中的一部分。

blocks.text: Some adults take classes for fun or because the class will be useful for them. Other adults take continuing education classes to improve their own lives because they want to feel better about themselves.
blocks.translation: 有些成年人上课是为了好玩，或因为课程对他们有用。另一些成年人参加继续教育课程是为了改善自己的生活，因为他们想对自己感觉更好。

blocks.text: Almost any community college or public school system has a continuing education program. There are classes in schools, community buildings or churches. Most classes are in the evening, so working people can attend. The classes are usually small, and they are inexpensive.
blocks.translation: 几乎任何社区学院或公立学校系统都有继续教育项目。课程设在学校、社区活动中心或教堂里。大多数课程在晚上进行，以便上班族参加。班级通常很小，费用也不高。

paragraphs: Ideas about education are changing in the United States. Education today is not just a high school diploma or a college degree. Many adults are not interested in going to college. They are interested in other kinds of learning. For them, learning does not end with a diploma.

Continuing education gives these adults the opportunity to increase their knowledge about their own field or to learn about a new field. It also gives them a chance to improve their old skills or to learn new ones.
Scientists, mechanics and barbers can take classes to improve their work skills. If they know more or learn more, they can get a better job or earn more money.

Continuing education classes give more adults the chances to learn new skills. There is usually a large variety of classes to choose from: typing, foreign cooking, photography, auto repair, furniture repair, or swimming. These are only some of the classes available.

Some adults take classes for fun or because the class will be useful for them. Other adults take continuing education classes to improve their own lives because they want to feel better about themselves.

Almost any community college or public school system has a continuing education program. There are classes in schools, community buildings or churches. Most classes are in the evening, so working people can attend. The classes are usually small, and they are inexpensive.

questions.stem: The new idea about education in the U.S. is that ______.
options: everyone should get a college degree
it’s no use for adults to go to college
a high school diploma is the end of education
adults should go on learning after graduating from school
questions.explanation: 第一段说教育不再只是文凭，许多成年人对其他学习方式感兴趣，“learning does not end with a diploma”，即毕业后仍应继续学习。
questions.evidence: learning does not end with a diploma

questions.stem: What’s the purpose for adults to continue their education?
options: Enlarge their knowledge and learn new skills.
Catch up the opportunity to get a higher degree.
Learn more basic knowledge to get a diploma.
Make themselves live a more comfortable life.
questions.explanation: 第二段说继续教育让成年人增加本领域知识、学习新领域，并提升旧技能或学习新技能。
questions.evidence: increase their knowledge ... improve their old skills or to learn new ones

questions.stem: Which of the following statement is true?
options: There are only a few continuing education classes available for adults.
Only those who want to get more money should go on with their education.
People take continuing education can get a good job.
All the people getting continuing education can get a good job.
questions.explanation: 第三段说如果学到更多，他们“can get a better job or earn more money”，因此 C 有原文依据；A、B、D 都过于绝对或与原文不符。
questions.evidence: they can get a better job or earn more money

questions.stem: Usually, the continuing education program is given ______.
options: in a small size and expensively
only in community buildings or churches
by community colleges and public schools
questions.explanation: 最后一段说几乎所有社区学院或公立学校系统都有继续教育项目，因此通常由社区学院和公立学校提供。
questions.evidence: Almost any community college or public school system has a continuing education program

questions.stem: The best title for the passage would be ______.
options: The Importance of a College Degree
A Good Way to Earn More Money
questions.explanation: 全文围绕继续教育课程（继续学习）、其目的、内容和提供方式展开，最佳标题是 Continuing Education Classes。

translations: 在美国，关于教育的观念正在发生变化。今天的教育不只是一张高中文凭或大学学位。许多成年人对上大学不感兴趣，他们感兴趣的是其他种类的学习。对他们来说，学习并不会随着拿到文凭而结束。
继续教育让这些成年人有机会增进本领域的知识，或学习一个新的领域。它也给他们机会提高旧技能或学习新技能。
科学家、机械师和理发师都可以上课来提高工作技能。如果他们懂得更多、学得更多，就能得到更好的工作或挣更多的钱。
继续教育课程让更多成年人有机会学习新技能。通常有各种各样的课程可供选择：打字、外国烹饪、摄影、汽车修理、家具修理或游泳。这些只是可选课程中的一部分。
有些成年人上课是为了好玩，或因为课程对他们有用。另一些成年人参加继续教育课程是为了改善自己的生活，因为他们想对自己感觉更好。
几乎任何社区学院或公立学校系统都有继续教育项目。课程设在学校、社区活动中心或教堂里。大多数课程在晚上进行，以便上班族参加。班级通常很小，费用也不高。

articles.title: No one knows exactly how many disabled people there are in the world, but estimates sugges
articles.fallbackTitle: No one knows exactly how many disabled people there are in the world, but estimates sugges

blocks.text: No one knows exactly how many disabled people there are in the world, but estimates suggest the number is over 450 million. The number of disabled people in India alone is probably more than double the total population of Canada.
blocks.translation: 没有人确切知道世界上有多少残疾人，但据估计这一数字超过 4.5 亿。仅印度的残疾人数就可能是加拿大总人口的两倍多。

blocks.text: In the United Kingdom, about one in ten people have some disability. Disability is not just something that happens to other people. As we get older, many of us will become less mobile, hard of hearing or have failing eyesight.
blocks.translation: 在英国，大约每十个人中就有一人有某种残疾。残疾并不只是发生在别人身上的事。随着年龄增长，我们中的许多人会变得行动不便、听力下降或视力衰退。

blocks.text: Disablement can take many forms and occur at any time of life. Some people are born with disabilities. Many others become disabled as they get older. There are many progressive disabling diseases. The longer time goes on, the worse they become. Some people are disabled in accidents. Many others may have a period of disability in the form of a mental illness. All are affected by people’s attitude towards them.
blocks.translation: 残疾有多种形式，可能发生在人生的任何阶段。有些人生来就有残疾，另有许多人随着年龄增长而致残。有许多渐进性的致残疾病，时间越久，病情越严重。有些人在事故中致残，还有许多人可能经历一段以精神疾病形式出现的残疾期。所有这些人都受到人们对他们态度的影响。

blocks.text: Disabled people face many physical barriers. Next time you go shopping or to work or visit friends, imagine how you would manage if you could not get up steps, or on to buses and trains. How would you cope if you could not see where you were going or could not hear the traffic? But there are other barriers: prejudice can be even harder to break down and ignorance inevitably represents by far the greatest barrier of all. It is almost impossible for the able-bodied to fully appreciate what the severely disabled go through, so it is important to draw attention to these barriers and show that it is the individual person and their ability, not their disability, which counts.
blocks.translation: 残疾人面临许多身体上的障碍。下次你去购物、上班或访友时，想象一下：如果你上不了台阶，上不了公交车和火车，你会怎么办？如果你看不见路，或听不见车流声，你会怎么应对？但还有其他障碍：偏见可能更难打破，而无知无疑是一切障碍中最大的。身体健全的人几乎不可能完全体会严重残疾者的经历，因此，提醒人们注意这些障碍，并表明真正重要的是个人及其能力、而不是其残疾，这一点至关重要。

paragraphs: No one knows exactly how many disabled people there are in the world, but estimates suggest the number is over 450 million. The number of disabled people in India alone is probably more than double the total population of Canada.

In the United Kingdom, about one in ten people have some disability. Disability is not just something that happens to other people. As we get older, many of us will become less mobile, hard of hearing or have failing eyesight.

Disablement can take many forms and occur at any time of life. Some people are born with disabilities. Many others become disabled as they get older. There are many progressive disabling diseases. The longer time goes on, the worse they become. Some people are disabled in accidents. Many others may have a period of disability in the form of a mental illness. All are affected by people’s attitude towards them.

Disabled people face many physical barriers. Next time you go shopping or to work or visit friends, imagine how you would manage if you could not get up steps, or on to buses and trains. How would you cope if you could not see where you were going or could not hear the traffic? But there are other barriers: prejudice can be even harder to break down and ignorance inevitably represents by far the greatest barrier of all. It is almost impossible for the able-bodied to fully appreciate what the severely disabled go through, so it is important to draw attention to these barriers and show that it is the individual person and their ability, not their disability, which counts.

在英国，大约每十个人中就有一人有某种残疾。残疾并不只是发生在别人身上的事。随着年龄增长，我们中的许多人会变得行动不便、听力下降或视力衰退。
残疾有多种形式，可能发生在人生的任何阶段。有些人生来就有残疾，另有许多人随着年龄增长而致残。有许多渐进性的致残疾病，时间越久，病情越严重。有些人在事故中致残，还有许多人可能经历一段以精神疾病形式出现的残疾期。所有这些人都受到人们对他们态度的影响。
残疾人面临许多身体上的障碍。下次你去购物、上班或访友时，想象一下：如果你上不了台阶，上不了公交车和火车，你会怎么办？如果你看不见路，或听不见车流声，你会怎么应对？但还有其他障碍：偏见可能更难打破，而无知无疑是一切障碍中最大的。身体健全的人几乎不可能完全体会严重残疾者的经历，因此，提醒人们注意这些障碍，并表明真正重要的是个人及其能力、而不是其残疾，这一点至关重要。

blocks.text: If we take a close look at successful language learners, we may discover a few techniques which make language learning easier for them.
blocks.translation: 如果我们仔细观察成功的语言学习者，可能会发现一些让语言学习对他们来说更容易的技巧。

blocks.text: First of all, successful language learners are independent learners. They do not depend on books or teachers; they discover their own way to learn the language. Instead of waiting for the teacher to explain everything, they try to find the patterns and the rules for themselves. They are good guessers who look for clues and form their own conclusions.
blocks.translation: 首先，成功的语言学习者是独立的学习者。他们不依赖书本或老师，而是自己摸索学习语言的方法。他们不等老师解释一切，而是自己努力找出模式和规则。他们善于猜测，会寻找线索并形成自己的结论。

blocks.text: Successful language learning is active learning. Therefore, successful learners do not wait for a chance to use the language; they look for such a chance. They find people who speak the language and ask these people to correct them when they make a mistake. They will try anything to communicate. When communication is difficult, they can accept information that is neither exact nor complete. It is more important for them to learn to think in the language than to know the meaning of every word.
blocks.translation: 成功的语言学习是主动的学习。因此，成功的学习者不会等待使用语言的机会，而是主动寻找这样的机会。他们找到说这种语言的人，并请这些人在自己犯错时纠正自己。他们会尝试一切办法来交流。当交流困难时，他们能够接受既不精确也不完整的信息。对他们来说，学会用这种语言思考，比知道每个词的意思更重要。

blocks.text: Finally, successful language learners are learners with a purpose. They want to learn the language because they are interested in the language and the people who speak it. It is necessary for them to learn the language in order to communicate with these people and to learn from them.
blocks.translation: 最后，成功的语言学习者是有目的的学习者。他们想学这门语言，是因为他们对这门语言以及说这种语言的人感兴趣。为了与这些人交流并向他们学习，他们有必要学会这门语言。

blocks.text: Most American people hate repeating the same work endlessly, especially those who live in the west of America. They try their best to make their life colorful and their work interesting. If they have to do the same regular work, they’ll try to do it in different ways. Repetition and Monotony(单调) are what they can’t stand.
blocks.translation: 大多数美国人讨厌无休止地重复同样的工作，尤其是住在美国西部的人。他们尽力让自己的生活丰富多彩、工作充满乐趣。如果不得不做同样的常规工作，他们会尝试用不同的方式去做。重复和单调是他们无法忍受的。

blocks.text: In the west of America, there is a beautiful old mountain village which is well known for its straw hats. The villagers there can make different styles of hats — hats for old gentlemen, for sweet and playful children, and for beautiful young ladies. People often go there to buy hats.
blocks.translation: 在美国西部，有一个美丽的古老山村，以草帽闻名。那里的村民能制作不同款式的帽子——给老年绅士的、给可爱顽皮孩子的，还有给漂亮年轻女士的。人们常去那里买帽子。

blocks.text: One day, there came a young tourist who entered a millinery(女士帽子)shop and found a very nice hat costing five dollars. He said to the shopkeeper, “If you agree to sell at a cheaper price, I’d like to buy two hundred hats of this style.” “No, you should pay me at least ten dollars each if you wish to get so many hats of the same style.” The tourist could not understand.
blocks.translation: 一天，来了一位年轻游客，他走进一家女帽店，看中了一顶非常漂亮的帽子，售价五美元。他对店主说：“如果你同意便宜点卖，我想买两百顶这种款式的帽子。”“不，如果你想买这么多同款帽子，至少得每顶付我十美元。”游客不明白。

blocks.text: “How’s that?”
blocks.translation: “怎么会这样？”

blocks.text: “Well, ” said the shopkeeper, “If you buy only one hat of this style, I can make it easily. If you order two hundred hats of different styles, I can also manage the business without much difficulty. However, it will almost bore me to death if you want me to make two hundred hats of the same style. So you at least pay me double price.”
blocks.translation: “嗯，”店主说，“如果你只买一顶这种款式的帽子，我做起来很容易。如果你订两百顶不同款式的帽子，我也能不太费力地应付。可是，如果你要我做出两百顶一模一样的帽子，那几乎会把我烦死。所以你至少得付我双倍的价钱。”

articles.title: It is exciting to apply for a job that really interests you
articles.fallbackTitle: It is exciting to apply for a job that really interests you

blocks.text: It is exciting to apply for a job that really interests you. In making your application, there are a number of points for you to observe.
blocks.translation: 申请一份你真正感兴趣的工作是令人兴奋的。在提出申请时，有几点需要注意。

blocks.text: In your letter of application, aim to say just enough to introduce yourself. If you are answering an advertisement, any information for which it asks must, of course, be given. This will usually cover your school record and any further education and training. You may also be asked to give the names of one or two persons to supply reference. For this purpose you should choose people who know enough about your character and ability; and you should also ask for their permission to be named as referees.
blocks.translation: 在求职信中，要力求恰到好处地介绍自己。如果你是在回应一则招聘广告，那么广告所要求的任何信息当然都必须提供。这通常包括你的在校成绩以及任何进一步的教育和培训经历。他们还可能要求你提供一两位证明人的姓名。为此，你应选择足够了解你品格和能力的人，并且应先征得他们同意，将其列为证明人。

blocks.text: It will depend on circumstances how much you can usefully add about yourself. Your purpose is to bring to the notice of the boss any good reason why you rather than any of the other applicants (申请人) should be chosen for the job. If you feel you have any special skill for the work or, for example, any particular interest in the line of the business, let this be known.
blocks.translation: 你能有效地补充多少关于自己的信息，要视情况而定。你的目的是让老板注意到你而非其他申请人、应当被选中担任这份工作的任何充分理由。如果你觉得自己在这项工作上有特殊技能，或者例如对这类行业有特别的兴趣，就应该让雇主知道。

blocks.text: Finally there is your use of language. You cannot go wrong if you keep your sentences and paragraphs short, making sure the sense is clear and well expressed. Choose plain words so long as they can express your meaning.
blocks.translation: 最后是语言的运用。只要你保持句子和段落简短，确保意思清楚、表达得体，就不会出错。只要能够表达你的意思，就选择朴实的词语。

articles.title: Unlike Britain, the United States does not have a national health care service
articles.fallbackTitle: Unlike Britain, the United States does not have a national health care service

blocks.text: Unlike Britain, the United States does not have a national health care service. The government does help pay for some medical care for people who are on low incomes and for old people, but most people buy insurance (保险) to help pay for medical care. The problems of those who cannot afford insurance are an important political subject.
blocks.translation: 与英国不同，美国没有全国性的医疗保健服务。政府确实会帮助低收入者和老年人支付部分医疗费用，但大多数人购买保险来帮助支付医疗费用。那些负担不起保险的人所面临的问题是一个重要的政治议题。

articles.title: Shopping for clothes is not the same experience for a man as it is for a woman
articles.fallbackTitle: Shopping for clothes is not the same experience for a man as it is for a woman

blocks.text: Shopping for clothes is not the same experience for a man as it is for a woman. A man goes shopping because he needs something. His purpose is clear and decided in advance. He knows what he wants, and his objective is to find it and buy it; the price is the second place for consideration (考虑). All men simply walk into a shop and ask the assistant for what they want. If the shop has it, the salesman quickly produces it, and the man begins to try it at once. For a man, the small problems may begin when the shop does not have what he wants, or does not have exactly what he wants. In that case the salesman will try to sell the customer something else. Very often, he offers the nearest thing that he can produce.
blocks.translation: 买衣服对男人和女人来说不是同一种体验。男人去购物是因为他需要某样东西。他的目的明确，而且是事先决定好的。他知道自己想要什么，目标是找到它并买下它；价格是第二位要考虑的因素。所有男人都会直接走进商店，向店员要他们想要的东西。如果店里有，售货员很快拿出来，男人马上开始试穿。对男人来说，小麻烦可能始于店里没有他想要的东西，或者没有完全符合他想要的东西。那种情况下，售货员会试图向顾客推销别的东西，而且常常拿出他能找到的最接近的东西。

blocks.text: Now how does a woman go about buying clothes? In almost every respect, she does so in the opposite way. Her shopping is not often based on need. She has never fully made up her mind about what she wants, and she is only “having a look round”. She will still be satisfied even if she has bought nothing.
blocks.translation: 那么女人是怎样买衣服的呢？几乎在每个方面，她的做法都相反。她购物通常不是出于需要。她从未完全想清楚自己想要什么，只是“随便看看”。即使什么也没买，她仍然会感到满足。

articles.title: The multi-billion-dollar Western pop music industry is under fire
articles.fallbackTitle: The multi-billion-dollar Western pop music industry is under fire

blocks.text: The multi-billion-dollar Western pop music industry is under fire. It is being blamed by the United Nations for the dramatic rise in drug abuse worldwide, “The most worrying development is a culture of drug-friendliness,” says the UN’s International Narcotics Control Board in a report released last year.
blocks.translation: 价值数十亿美元的西方流行音乐产业正受到抨击。联合国指责它导致全世界吸毒现象急剧增加。联合国国际麻醉品管制局在去年发布的一份报告中说：“最令人担忧的事态发展是一种对毒品友好的文化。”

blocks.text: The 74-page study says the pop music, as a global industry, is by far the most influential trend-setter for young people of most cultures. “Some songs encourage people to take drugs. Certain pop stars make statements and set examples as if the use of drugs for non-medicinal purposes were a normal and acceptable part of a person’s lifestyle,” the study says.
blocks.translation: 这份 74 页的研究报告指出，流行音乐作为一个全球产业，迄今为止是大多数文化中年轻人最具影响力的潮流引领者。报告说：“一些歌曲鼓励人们吸毒。某些流行歌星发表言论、树立榜样，仿佛非医疗用途使用毒品是人们生活方式中正常且可接受的一部分。”

blocks.text: Surprisingly, says the Board, the effect of drug-friendly pop music seems to survive despite the occasional shock of death by overdose. “Such incidents tend to be seen as an occasion to mourn the loss of a role model, and not an opportunity to face the deadly effect of drug use,” it notes. Since the 1970s, several internationally famous singers and movie stars — including Elvis Presley, Janice Joplin, John Belushi, Jimi Hendrix, Jonathan Melvin and Andy Gibbs — have died of either drug abuse or drug related illnesses. With the globalization of popular music — messages promoting drug abuse are now reaching beyond their countries of origin. “In most countries, the names of certain pop stars have become familiar to the members of every household,” the study says.
blocks.translation: 该机构表示，令人惊讶的是，尽管偶尔发生吸毒过量致死的震惊事件，对毒品友好的流行音乐的影响似乎依然存在。报告指出：“这类事件往往被视为悼念失去偶像的场合，而不是正视吸毒致命后果的机会。”自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，几位国际知名歌手和影星——包括埃尔维斯·普雷斯利、贾尼斯·乔普林、约翰·贝鲁西、吉米·亨德里克斯、乔纳森·梅尔文和安迪·吉布斯——死于吸毒或与毒品相关的疾病。随着流行音乐的全球化，宣扬吸毒的信息如今已传播到原产国之外。报告说：“在大多数国家，某些流行歌星的名字已为家家户户所熟悉。”

blocks.text: The UN study also blames the media for its description of certain drug incidents, which encourages rather than prevents drug abuse. “Over the past years, we have seen how drug abuse is increasingly regarded as being acceptable or even attractive,” says Hamid Ghodse, president of the Board. “Powerful pressure groups run political campaigns aimed at legalizing controlled drugs,” he says. Ghodse also points out that all these developments have created an environment which is tolerant of or even favorable to drug abuse and spoils international drug prevention efforts currently under way.
blocks.translation: 联合国的研究还指责媒体对某些毒品事件的描述，这种描述鼓励而非阻止吸毒。“过去几年，我们看到吸毒越来越被视为可接受甚至具有吸引力，”该机构主席哈米德·戈德塞说。“势力强大的压力集团开展政治运动，旨在使受管制毒品合法化，”他说。戈德塞还指出，所有这些事态发展营造了一种宽容甚至纵容吸毒的环境，破坏了目前正在进行的国际禁毒努力。

blocks.text: The study focuses on demand reduction and prevention within an environment that has become tolerant of drug abuse. The Board calls on governments to do their legal and moral duties, and to act against the pro-drug-abuse messages of the youth culture to which young people are increasingly being exposed.
blocks.translation: 这项研究重点关注在一个已变得宽容吸毒的环境中减少需求和预防吸毒。该机构呼吁各国政府履行法律和道德义务，并针对青年文化中宣扬吸毒的信息采取行动，因为年轻人正越来越多地接触这些信息。

articles.title: The food we eat seems to have profound effects on our health
articles.fallbackTitle: The food we eat seems to have profound effects on our health

blocks.text: The food we eat seems to have profound effects on our health. Although science has made enormous steps in making food more fit to eat, it has, at the same time, made many foods unfit to eat. Some research has shown that perhaps eighty percent of all human illnesses are related to diet and forty percent of cancer is related to the diet as well, especially cancer of the colon. Different cultures are more likely to cause certain different illnesses because of the food that is characteristic in these cultures. That food is related to illness is a new discovery. In 1945, government researchers realized that nitrates, commonly used to preserve color in meats, and other food additives, caused cancer. Yet, these carcinogenic additives remain in our food, and it becomes more difficult all the time to know which things on the packaging labels of processed food are helpful or harmful.
blocks.translation: 我们吃的食物似乎对我们的健康有深远影响。尽管科学在使食物更适合食用方面取得了巨大进步，但与此同时，也让许多食物变得不宜食用。一些研究表明，人类所有疾病中或许有 80% 与饮食有关，40% 的癌症也与饮食有关，尤其是结肠癌。不同文化更可能引发某些不同的疾病，因为这些文化中有其特色的食物。食物与疾病有关是一个新发现。1945 年，政府研究人员意识到，常用于保持肉类色泽的硝酸盐和其他食品添加剂会致癌。然而，这些致癌添加剂仍留在我们的食物中，而且要知道加工食品包装标签上的哪些东西有益、哪些有害，变得越来越困难。

blocks.text: The additives which we eat are not all so direct. Farmers often give penicillin to beef and living animals, and because of this, penicillin has been found in the milk of treated cows. Some times similar drugs are given to animals not for medical purposes, but for financial reasons. The farmers are simply trying to fatten the animals in order to obtain a higher price on the market. Although the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has tried repeatedly to control these procedures, the practices continue.

paragraphs: The food we eat seems to have profound effects on our health. Although science has made enormous steps in making food more fit to eat, it has, at the same time, made many foods unfit to eat. Some research has shown that perhaps eighty percent of all human illnesses are related to diet and forty percent of cancer is related to the diet as well, especially cancer of the colon. Different cultures are more likely to cause certain different illnesses because of the food that is characteristic in these cultures. That food is related to illness is a new discovery. In 1945, government researchers realized that nitrates, commonly used to preserve color in meats, and other food additives, caused cancer. Yet, these carcinogenic additives remain in our food, and it becomes more difficult all the time to know which things on the packaging labels of processed food are helpful or harmful.

The additives which we eat are not all so direct. Farmers often give penicillin to beef and living animals, and because of this, penicillin has been found in the milk of treated cows. blocks.text: Choosing a college requires that you ask yourself many questions. Who do you want to be? What do you want to do? Where do you want to go in life? How do you get there? Perhaps the best way to find those answers is to look at our college on Long Island.
blocks.translation: 选择大学需要你问自己许多问题。你想成为什么样的人？你想做什么？你想在人生中走向何方？你如何到达那里？也许找到这些答案的最好方法，是来看看我们这所位于长岛的大学。

blocks.text: Think about it. Private colleges on Long Island charge an average of $25, 000 a year on overall costs, an average total of $100, 000 over four years. Our college’s cost is just over $13, 000 or about $53, 000 over four years. That means, because of the investment of the State of New York in our public college, you pay nearly half what students at those private colleges pay. That’s the money you can use later for graduate school, travel, or whatever you choose.
blocks.translation: 想一想：长岛私立大学的总体费用平均每年 25,000 美元，四年平均总计 100,000 美元。而我们大学的费用仅略高于 13,000 美元，四年约 53,000 美元。这意味着，由于纽约州对我们这所公立大学的投入，你支付的费用几乎是那些私立大学学生的一半。这笔钱你以后可以用于读研究生、旅行或任何你选择的事情。

articles.title: There has been an ongoing debate on whether school uniforms should be completely abolished
articles.fallbackTitle: There has been an ongoing debate on whether school uniforms should be completely abolished

blocks.text: There has been an ongoing debate on whether school uniforms should be completely abolished in all schools, both private and public. Despite both pros and cons（赞同和反对意见）of any uniform, personally I stick to the idea that school uniforms should be introduced in all public and private schools.
blocks.translation: 关于是否应在所有学校（包括私立和公立学校）彻底废除校服，一直存在争论。尽管校服有利有弊，但我个人坚持认为，所有公立和私立学校都应引入校服。

blocks.text: There are certainly many factors that should be taken into account when discussing the issue of school uniforms. While most private schools already have established a particular school uniform to be worn at all times and by all students, public schools mostly remain more liberal and only have a more or less strict dress code. In public schools, some kids have parents with rather high incomes who can afford to buy fashionable and costly clothes for their kids. But there are also those teens who are forced to buy low-cost outfits at discount retail stores. If all students wear identical clothes, no one will be hurt by the comparison.
blocks.translation: 讨论校服问题时，当然有许多因素需要考虑。大多数私立学校已经规定所有学生在任何时候都必须穿某种特定的校服，而公立学校大多更为自由，只有或多或少严格的着装规定。在公立学校，有些孩子的父母收入相当高，能给孩子买时髦昂贵的衣服；但也有一些青少年不得不在折扣零售店购买廉价服装。如果所有学生都穿同样的衣服，就不会有人因攀比而受到伤害。

blocks.text: Another point to consider is, of course, the way teenagers try to express their feelings. If from an early age children get used to paying too much attention to the way people dress and look instead of enriching their inner being and acquiring new skills, we should expect a very materialistic（物质至上的）society in the nearest future. Wearing a uniform would help in having people pay more attention to one’s personality, rather than looks. The main idea is to help a child understand that they should develop their inner beauty and not get involved with bad company and false friends.
blocks.translation: 当然，另一点需要考虑的是青少年表达情感的方式。如果孩子从小就习惯于过分关注人们的穿着和外表，而不是充实内在、学习新技能，那么我们预计在不久的将来会看到一个非常物质至上的社会。穿校服有助于让人们更多关注一个人的品格，而不是外表。其核心思想是帮助孩子明白，他们应该发展内在美，不要与不良伙伴和虚假的朋友混在一起。

blocks.text: All in all, wearing school uniforms is a great solution to these arguments. What counts most is that school uniforms teach children a certain discipline — the qualities they will later in life make use of when they have to obey certain social norms and laws.
blocks.translation: 总而言之，穿校服是解决这些争论的好办法。最重要的是，校服教会孩子一定的纪律——这些品质在他们以后必须遵守社会规范和律法时会派上用场。

paragraphs: There has been an ongoing debate on whether school uniforms should be completely abolished in all schools, both private and public. Despite both pros and cons（赞同和反对意见）of any uniform, personally I stick to the idea that school uniforms should be introduced in all public and private schools.

There are certainly many factors that should be taken into account when discussing the issue of school uniforms. While most private schools already have established a particular school uniform to be worn at all times and by all students, public schools mostly remain more liberal and only have a more or less strict dress code. In public schools, some kids have parents with rather high incomes who can afford to buy fashionable and costly clothes for their kids. But there are also those teens who are forced to buy low-cost outfits at discount retail stores. If all students wear identical clothes, no one will be hurt by the comparison.

Another point to consider is, of course, the way teenagers try to express their feelings. If from an early age children get used to paying too much attention to the way people dress and look instead of enriching their inner being and acquiring new skills, we should expect a very materialistic（物质至上的）society in the nearest future. Wearing a uniform would help in having people pay more attention to one’s personality, rather than looks. The main idea is to help a child understand that they should develop their inner beauty and not get involved with bad company and false friends.

All in all, wearing school uniforms is a great solution to these arguments. What counts most is that school uniforms teach children a certain discipline — the qualities they will later in life make use of when they have to obey certain social norms and laws.

translations: 关于是否应在所有学校（包括私立和公立学校）彻底废除校服，一直存在争论。尽管校服有利有弊，但我个人坚持认为，所有公立和私立学校都应引入校服。
讨论校服问题时，当然有许多因素需要考虑。大多数私立学校已经规定所有学生在任何时候都必须穿某种特定的校服，而公立学校大多更为自由，只有或多或少严格的着装规定。在公立学校，有些孩子的父母收入相当高，能给孩子买时髦昂贵的衣服；但也有一些青少年不得不在折扣零售店购买廉价服装。如果所有学生都穿同样的衣服，就不会有人因攀比而受到伤害。
当然，另一点需要考虑的是青少年表达情感的方式。如果孩子从小就习惯于过分关注人们的穿着和外表，而不是充实内在、学习新技能，那么我们预计在不久的将来会看到一个非常物质至上的社会。穿校服有助于让人们更多关注一个人的品格，而不是外表。其核心思想是帮助孩子明白，他们应该发展内在美，不要与不良伙伴和虚假的朋友混在一起。
总而言之，穿校服是解决这些争论的好办法。最重要的是，校服教会孩子一定的纪律——这些品质在他们以后必须遵守社会规范和律法时会派上用场。

blocks.text: Scientists can learn about man by studying animals, such as mice, rats and monkeys. The scientists in a laboratory are experimenting on mice and they are studying the relationship between diet and health.
blocks.translation: 科学家可以通过研究老鼠、大鼠和猴子等动物来了解人类。实验室里的科学家正在用老鼠做实验，研究饮食与健康之间的关系。

blocks.text: In this experiment, the scientists are studying the relationship between the amount of food the mice can eat and their health. The mice are in three groups. All these groups are receiving the same healthy diet. But the amount of food that each group is receiving is different. The first group is eating one cup of food each day, the second two cups, and the third three cups.
blocks.translation: 在这个实验中，科学家正在研究老鼠能吃的食物量与健康之间的关系。老鼠分为三组。所有组都吃同样的健康食物，但每组获得的食物量不同。第一组每天吃一杯食物，第二组两杯，第三组三杯。

blocks.text: After three years, the healthiest group is the one that is only eating one cup of food each day. The mice in this group are thinner than normal mice but they are more active. Most of the day, they are running, playing with one another, and using the equipment in their cages. Also, they are living longer. Mice usually live for two years, while most of the mice in this group are still alive after three years.
blocks.translation: 三年后，最健康的是每天只吃一杯食物的那一组。这组老鼠比正常老鼠瘦，但更活跃。一天中大部分时间，它们都在跑动、互相玩耍，使用笼子里的设备。而且它们活得更久。老鼠通常活两年，而这组的大多数老鼠三年后仍然活着。

blocks.text: The second group of mice is of normal weight. They are healthy, too. They are active, but not as active as the thinner mice. But they are only living about two years.
blocks.translation: 第二组老鼠体重正常。它们也健康，很活跃，但不如那些较瘦的老鼠活跃。不过它们只活了大约两年。

blocks.text: The last group of mice is receiving more food than the other two groups. Most of the day, these mice are eating or sleeping. They are not active. These mice are living longer than the scientists thought — about a year and a half, but they are not healthy. They are sick more often than the other two groups.
blocks.translation: 最后一组老鼠获得的食物比其他两组多。一天中大部分时间，这些老鼠不是在吃就是在睡。它们不活跃。这些老鼠比科学家预想的活得久——大约一年半，但它们不健康，生病的次数比其他两组多。

blocks.text: The number of international students at colleges and universities in the United States has increased continually for the fifth year.
blocks.translation: 美国高校的国际学生人数已连续第五年增长。

blocks.text: The Institute of International Education in New York released its annual “Open Doors” report this week. It says a record of more than 720, 000 students from other countries were studying in America during the last school year. The number was 5% higher than the year before and almost one-third higher than ten years ago.
blocks.translation: 纽约的国际教育协会本周发布了年度《门户开放》报告。报告称，上一学年有超过 72 万名来自其他国家的学生在美国学习，创下纪录。这一数字比前一年高 5%，比十年前高近三分之一。

blocks.text: There were big increases from China, Saudi Arabia, Vietnam, Iran and Venezuela. Almost 22% of international students were Chinese, with increases especially at the undergraduate level. Together, almost half of all international students came from China, India and South Korea.
blocks.translation: 来自中国、沙特阿拉伯、越南、伊朗和委内瑞拉的学生人数大幅增加。近 22% 的国际学生是中国人，本科阶段的增长尤为明显。来自中国、印度和韩国的学生合计占所有国际学生的近一半。

blocks.text: Peggy Blumenthal at the institute says that Chinese students are now studying throughout the United States. Twenty years ago, students from China only knew of a handful of the US institutions, but now they are admitted into the US community colleges, small liberal arts institutions, and research universities — really spread across the US. Ms. Blumenthal suggests that one reason for the increase is a lack of space in Chinese colleges for everyone who wants an education. She says students and their parents are also looking for a different educational experience.
blocks.translation: 该协会的佩吉·布卢门撒尔说，中国学生现在遍布美国各地学习。二十年前，中国学生只知道少数几所美国院校，但现在他们被美国的社区学院、小型文理学院和研究型大学录取——真正遍布全美。布卢门撒尔女士认为，人数增加的一个原因是中国大学没有足够的名额容纳所有想接受教育的人。她说，学生和家长也在寻求不同的教育体验。

blocks.text: The most popular area of study for international students is business and management, followed by engineering.

articles.heading: Step 1: Use open-ended questions
articles.title: Step 1: Use open-ended questions
articles.fallbackTitle: For a conversation to flow well, it’s important to ask open questions; these often start w

blocks.text: For a conversation to flow well, it’s important to ask open questions; these often start with “how”, “when”, “why”, etc. Try to avoid asking closed questions that can be answered with yes or no answers, because closed questions tend to kill the conversation.
blocks.translation: 要让对话顺畅进行，提出开放式问题很重要；这类问题常以“如何”“何时”“为什么”等开头。尽量避免问可以用是或否回答的封闭式问题，因为封闭式问题往往会扼杀对话。

blocks.text: Step 2: Listen actively
blocks.translation: 第 2 步：积极倾听

blocks.text: People speak at 100 to 175 words per minute, but they can listen intelligently at up to 300 words per minute. Since only a part of our mind is paying attention, it is easy to go into mind drift — thinking about other things while listening to someone. The cure for this is active listening, which involves listening with a purpose.
blocks.translation: 人们说话的速度是每分钟 100 到 175 个词，但我们可以每分钟听懂多达 300 个词。由于我们只动用了一部分注意力，很容易走神——在听别人说话时想着别的事情。解决办法是积极倾听，也就是有目的地听。

blocks.text: Step 3: Create a “cocoon”
blocks.translation: 第 3 步：营造一个“茧”

blocks.text: If you’re finding it particularly difficult to concentrate on what someone is saying, try to imagine a “cocoon” around you and the person you’re listening to. Imagine that the cocoon is blocking out all outside distractions（干扰）, so you can really focus on what they are saying.
blocks.translation: 如果你发现自己特别难以集中注意力听别人说话，试着想象一个“茧”把你自己和你正在听的人包围起来。想象这个茧挡住了所有外界干扰，这样你就能真正专注于对方说的话。

blocks.text: Step 4: Engage with the other person
blocks.translation: 第 4 步：与对方互动

blocks.text: When someone is trying to get your attention, or engage you in a conversation, don’t turn your back on them or answer over your shoulder. Instead, turn and face them, engage with them. Good communication is when you really engage. When you are talking to people, observe your body language and your tone of voice. Remember to use gestures, look people in the eye and smile when you talk unless you are complaining about something.
blocks.translation: 当有人想引起你的注意或让你参与对话时，不要背对着他们，也不要头也不回地应付。相反，要转过身面对他们，与他们互动。良好的沟通在于真正的投入。与人交谈时，注意你的肢体语言和语气。记住在说话时使用手势、看着对方的眼睛并微笑，除非你是在抱怨某事。

paragraphs: For a conversation to flow well, it’s important to ask open questions; these often start with “how”, “when”, “why”, etc. Try to avoid asking closed questions that can be answered with yes or no answers, because closed questions tend to kill the conversation.
Step 2: Listen actively

People speak at 100 to 175 words per minute, but they can listen intelligently at up to 300 words per minute. Since only a part of our mind is paying attention, it is easy to go into mind drift — thinking about other things while listening to someone. The cure for this is active listening, which involves listening with a purpose.
Step 3: Create a “cocoon”

If you’re finding it particularly difficult to concentrate on what someone is saying, try to imagine a “cocoon” around you and the person you’re listening to. Imagine that the cocoon is blocking out all outside distractions（干扰）, so you can really focus on what they are saying.
Step 4: Engage with the other person

When someone is trying to get your attention, or engage you in a conversation, don’t turn your back on them or answer over your shoulder. Instead, turn and face them, engage with them. Good communication is when you really engage. When you are talking to people, observe your body language and your tone of voice. Remember to use gestures, look people in the eye and smile when you talk unless you are complaining about something.

options: Mind drift and engaging in conversations.
questions.explanation: 文章给出四个改善沟通的技巧：开放问题、积极倾听、创造专注空间、投入互动，主题是 communication skills。

translations: 要让对话顺畅进行，提出开放式问题很重要；这类问题常以“如何”“何时”“为什么”等开头。尽量避免问可以用是或否回答的封闭式问题，因为封闭式问题往往会扼杀对话。
第 2 步：积极倾听
人们说话的速度是每分钟 100 到 175 个词，但我们可以每分钟听懂多达 300 个词。由于我们只动用了一部分注意力，很容易走神——在听别人说话时想着别的事情。解决办法是积极倾听，也就是有目的地听。
第 3 步：营造一个“茧”
如果你发现自己特别难以集中注意力听别人说话，试着想象一个“茧”把你自己和你正在听的人包围起来。想象这个茧挡住了所有外界干扰，这样你就能真正专注于对方说的话。
第 4 步：与对方互动
当有人想引起你的注意或让你参与对话时，不要背对着他们，也不要头也不回地应付。相反，要转过身面对他们，与他们互动。良好的沟通在于真正的投入。与人交谈时，注意你的肢体语言和语气。记住在说话时使用手势、看着对方的眼睛并微笑，除非你是在抱怨某事。

Some performance-supporting sugars are found in all kinds of healthy fruits. That’s why NBA All-Star Carmelo Anthony has adopted a diet（饮食）filled with fruits to stay within his weight range of 228-230 pounds. blocks.text: The first forest library in Shanghai recently opened to the public. Known as Read \& Joy Forest, the library was jointly founded by Pudong New Area and Shanghai Library. It is located in an urban wood, covering an area of 20, 546 square meters.
blocks.translation: 上海首个森林图书馆最近向公众开放。这座图书馆名为“悦读森林”，由浦东新区和上海图书馆共同创办。它位于一片城市林地中，占地 20,546 平方米。

blocks.text: The design of forest library allows an environment-friendly principle — ensuring minimum disturbance to nature, with existing green spaces connected by wooden walkways.
blocks.translation: 森林图书馆的设计遵循环保原则——确保对自然的干扰最小，用木制步道连接现有的绿地。

blocks.text: The library is can be open air and equipped with facilities such as benches and an information booth. Visitors can read and relax in a natural environment. It allows visitors to take a pleasant walk in the quiet forest, which includes osmanthus.
blocks.translation: 这座图书馆可以是露天的，配备长椅和信息亭等设施。游客可以在自然环境中阅读和放松。它让游客能在安静的森林中愉快散步，林中还有桂花。

blocks.translation: 在上海图书馆工作的徐强认为，在森林里设图书馆是室内阅读的延伸。“它给读者提供了一种不同的阅读体验，”他补充道。
